claims.capability: Synchronize POS orders and inventory with Shopify admin and other active sales channels
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can see in-person orders and inventory updates in the shared Shopify admin across retail locations and channels.
claims.trigger: A POS sale or restock is recorded at a selected location.
claims.behavior: Shopify POS syncs orders and inventory with Shopify admin across retail locations, online store, and other active channels.
preconditions: Multi-location is activated in store settings for POS use.
qualifiers: POS app is available on iOS and Android.
recovery_edge_cases: No sync timing or conflict-recovery guarantee was established by the inspected overview.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: A merchant-controlled local transaction journal with explicit sync status and conflict explanations could make cross-location reconciliation easier; measure unresolved sync exceptions per 1,000 sales.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Currency settlement is separate from the documented catalog/order synchronization behavior; a Bitcoin-enabled system could preserve the same multi-channel inventory job. Measure successful reconciliation for cash, card, and Bitcoin tenders without forced fiat conversion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A distributed payment ledger does not by itself provide Shopify's catalog or channel sync; merchants still need inventory authority and clear reconciliation semantics.
claims.acceptance_test: Record one POS sale and one restock at a selected location; verify both appear against that location in admin and the linked inventory/order views.

claims.capability: Create product records and represent options as variants
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can add a product to the catalog and represent color or size choices under one product.
claims.actor: Merchant using Shopify admin or Shopify app
claims.trigger: Merchant adds a product or needs another option for an existing item.
claims.behavior: Merchant saves a product with title and other details; for options such as color/size, Shopify directs merchant to add a variant rather than duplicate the product.
preconditions: Product is edited in Shopify admin or Shopify app.
qualifiers: For stores with more than 50 locations, product must be saved before inventory quantities are added.
recovery_edge_cases: Product duplication creates an independent product, and active duplicates publish to the same sales channels as the original unless staged as draft.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: A POS-oriented catalog flow could expose variant completeness and location availability before publishing; measure product setup corrections after first sale.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Catalog identity and variant selection are tender-independent; test that the same variant can be sold with Bitcoin while stock and order identity remain intact.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No payment behavior is implied by variant management; a Bitcoin payment option must not require a duplicate product or force fiat conversion.
claims.acceptance_test: Create a product, add a size or color option as a variant, and verify the product remains a single catalog record with selectable variant details.

claims.capability: View inventory state for product at a POS location
claims.merchant_outcome: Staff can inspect whether stock is available, committed, unavailable, or incoming before making inventory decisions.
claims.trigger: Staff searches for a product and opens its details.
claims.behavior: POS product details display available, committed, unavailable, and incoming quantities; selected location determines its location context.
preconditions: Inventory tracking enabled in admin and inventory assigned to locations.
qualifiers: Staff may view inventory for all locations even when PIN access is restricted by location.
recovery_edge_cases: If inventory tracking is not enabled or no stock is assigned to a location, counts cannot be relied on as tracked location stock.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show stock provenance and last-update time beside each quantity to help staff spot stale counts; measure inventory discrepancies caught before sale.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Stock visibility should behave identically regardless of tender; measure whether Bitcoin sales consume the same location stock exactly once.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Payment settlement does not supply stock truth; the merchant's inventory system remains the operational authority.
claims.acceptance_test: At a location with tracked stock, inspect a product and confirm the four documented stock states and selected-location context.

claims.capability: Record physical counts and adjust POS inventory quantities
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can reconcile a physical count against recorded on-hand quantity.
claims.trigger: A scheduled or ad hoc physical count identifies a quantity discrepancy.
claims.behavior: Shopify POS uses the Quick counts POS UI extension for direct quantity adjustment; admin also supports inventory page, bulk editor, and CSV export/import adjustments.
preconditions: Inventory tracking is enabled and location stock assigned for tracked inventory.
qualifiers: Quick counts is a POS UI extension, not the base POS workflow described here; admin adjustments are separate paths.
recovery_edge_cases: Guide recommends counting when retail outlets are closed and online sales are not peaking to reduce concurrent-change discrepancy risk.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: A count flow with reason codes and discrepancy review could improve auditability; measure count-to-ledger variance and time to resolve.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Inventory correction is tender-independent; verify a Bitcoin sale decrements the same stock ledger and count adjustment reconciles it without a separate fiat-only workflow.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No Bitcoin-specific inventory behavior is documented; payment acceptance cannot replace physical count controls.
claims.acceptance_test: Using a configured count tool or admin adjustment path, enter a physical count and confirm the corrected quantity is reflected for that location.

claims.capability: Fulfill an admin-created transfer from origin POS location
claims.merchant_outcome: Origin staff can pick/pack and send all or partial quantities to another retail location while recording stock movement.
claims.trigger: An inventory transfer has been created in Shopify admin and is ready to ship.
claims.behavior: Staff create a shipment, scan or enter item quantities, then send it; inventory counts update and destination is notified.
preconditions: POS Pro location; Inventory and Manage transfers permissions; active internet connection; transfer pre-created in admin.
qualifiers: POS cannot create the transfer or purchase/print a shipping label.
recovery_edge_cases: Guide allows incremental multiple shipments; packing slip is optional and requires POS Pro, POS app v11.6+, and connected/AirPrint-compatible printer.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: A scan-first shipment confirmation with discrepancy prompts could reduce mis-picks; measure transfer quantity corrections at destination.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Internal stock movement does not depend on payment rail; a Bitcoin POS should preserve transfer handling and must not force a conversion or extra payment step.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Transfer coordination and shipping remain operational workflows distinct from settlement; the guide's admin-first setup and connectivity requirements remain relevant.
claims.acceptance_test: Create an admin transfer, scan or enter a partial shipment at origin, send it, then verify shipment state and location stock update.

claims.capability: Review and accept/reject incoming transfer quantities at destination
claims.merchant_outcome: Destination staff can match received stock to shipped quantities and update destination inventory.
claims.trigger: A transfer shipment arrives in transit.
claims.behavior: Current built-in transfer flow lets staff accept all, review shipments individually, or count/scan line items and accept a quantity; Shopify admin also has native linked-transfer receipt actions. Legacy Stocky extension page documented accepted/rejected item flow but is no longer current.
preconditions: Current POS fulfill/receive requires POS Pro, transfer created in admin, Inventory and Manage transfers permissions and internet. Admin receipt requires transfer access.
qualifiers: Stocky Transfers POS UI extension is historical: Stocky ended 2026-08-31; current POS receipt is documented in standard transfer workflow, while current supplier PO receiving guide specifies admin linked-transfer receipt.
recovery_edge_cases: Legacy Stocky accepted amounts could not be undone in POS; standard transfer flow allows review options and partial receipt. Do not apply the historical Stocky irreversibility rule to current native admin receiving without evidence.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Explicitly surface irreversible acceptance where applicable and provide count discrepancy summary before save; measure corrected receipts and accidental acceptance reports.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Receipt workflow is tender-independent; verify Bitcoin-funded retail sales and standard receipts share the same received stock ledger.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Payment method does not make an inventory receipt reversible; receiving controls and permissions remain merchant responsibilities.
claims.acceptance_test: Receive an inbound location transfer with a mismatch, reject or adjust a line item, save, and verify received location quantity and transfer status.

claims.capability: Create a customer profile and record marketing preference from POS cart
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can retain customer details for later orders and record the customer's marketing choice.
claims.trigger: Customer agrees to provide contact details during a sale or future-order setup.
claims.behavior: Staff enter at least one of first name, last name, email, or phone to create a profile and can turn marketing acceptance on or off; profile can be saved without attaching to current cart.
preconditions: POS app is online for customer search/edit/create workflows.
qualifiers: Profile can include contact data, notes, addresses, tax status, tags and marketing choice; custom metafields are configured in admin.
recovery_edge_cases: Customer may be saved without adding to cart; offline staff cannot create or edit customer profiles.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make consent capture provenance and purpose visible at entry; measure profile completion and consent corrections without increasing checkout time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Customer profile and consent behavior should not depend on tender; test equivalent profile linking for Bitcoin transactions and avoid requiring unnecessary identity for payment acceptance.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Customer data is not required by the cited payment-independent profile flow; preserve data minimization and do not couple Bitcoin payment to identity capture.
claims.acceptance_test: Create a profile from POS with marketing disabled, optionally save without attaching to the cart, and verify the recorded preference.

claims.capability: Associate a recognized chip-card customer name with a completed POS order
claims.merchant_outcome: Staff may identify a repeat customer after payment without manually entering their name at checkout.
claims.trigger: A customer pays with a recognized chip card and Shopify Payments is activated.
claims.behavior: When the card/network shares cardholder first and last name, POS can automatically create a name-only customer profile on the order; contactless cards do not share a name and do not create this profile.
preconditions: Shopify Payments activated; recognized chip-card transaction and card network supplies name.
qualifiers: This is contingent card-network data behavior, not guaranteed for all cards; profile initially contains only name.
recovery_edge_cases: Staff can later add contact details by editing profile in POS or admin; no automatic profile from contactless tap is documented.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Clearly disclose when payment-derived profile data is available and offer a merchant-configurable review step; measure mistaken or unwanted customer associations.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: A Bitcoin flow should allow optional customer association without borrowing card-network identity data; compare repeat-customer matching utility against privacy and avoid forced identity capture.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Card rails may provide a name signal some merchants find useful; Bitcoin does not inherently supply that customer identity, so merchants may need an explicit opt-in profile flow.
claims.acceptance_test: Compare documented outcome for recognized chip card vs contactless card: only the recognized-name case should produce the conditional name-only profile.

claims.capability: Issue digital or physical gift cards through Shopify POS
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can sell a stored-value gift instrument in person in digital, printed, or physical pre-coded form.
claims.trigger: Customer requests purchase of a gift card.
claims.behavior: Staff use Add gift card tile and select digital or physical where applicable; formats include emailed digital, printed digital receipt, or physical card with pre-assigned code.
preconditions: Gift cards are available on all Shopify subscription plans; physical pre-assigned-code issuance setting must be activated; market-specific local currency gift card must match configured POS market.
qualifiers: Physical Shopify hardware-store card availability is country-limited; third-party physical card code must be 8–20 alphanumeric characters.
recovery_edge_cases: Guide prerequisites distinguish card formats and physical-code setup; selling gift cards offline is not established here.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show card format, destination, and denomination confirmation before issuing value; measure issuance corrections and failed delivery.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: A merchant could explore Bitcoin-denominated gift value alongside the existing stored-value job; prove redemption, liability accounting, and customer display are correct without forced conversion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Gift-card balances are merchant liabilities and may depend on currency, jurisdiction, and platform accounting; a Bitcoin-denominated version changes valuation and redemption handling and is not implied by the guide.
claims.acceptance_test: Issue an emailed digital and a pre-coded physical card in supported configuration; verify format and issued code/value are visible to the merchant and customer.

claims.capability: Attribute POS activity to individual staff identity via PIN
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can associate orders and register activity with the staff member who used the POS.
claims.trigger: A staff member unlocks an initialized POS device and performs actions.
claims.behavior: Each POS staff member has a unique 4–6 digit PIN; actions including orders and register activity are associated with the PIN-entering staff member.
preconditions: An eligible user with admin and POS access initially logs into the device; staff has POS access and location permission.
qualifiers: PIN is identity attribution, while permissions are managed separately; Lite and Pro role behavior differs.
recovery_edge_cases: After five incorrect PIN attempts, next attempt is blocked for 30 seconds; a changed PIN may take minutes to sync and device may need internet refresh.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Add clear last-used identity and quick PIN recovery cues while preserving individual attribution; measure shared-PIN incidents and lockout support requests.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Staff attribution is payment-rail-neutral; ensure Bitcoin transactions carry the same staff actor linkage as cash/card sales.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: PIN attribution does not prove who physically authorized an external wallet transaction; retain transaction-specific approval and audit evidence.
claims.acceptance_test: Two staff unlock with separate PINs and complete actions; verify each action is attributed to the correct staff profile.

claims.capability: Assign role-based access to POS tasks at Pro locations
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can give staff reusable permission sets and require approval for selected sensitive actions.
claims.trigger: Merchant creates/assigns a role or staff attempts a restricted action.
claims.behavior: At POS Pro locations, staff receive a POS role comprising permissions; roles can restrict actions such as returns, discounts, or cash tracking, and manager approval can authorize gated actions by PIN.
preconditions: POS Pro for POS roles; authorized role administrator assigns role.
qualifiers: POS Lite does not apply POS roles; a staff member with access to Lite may have full POS access there. POS-only staff require Pro.
recovery_edge_cases: Role edits do not extend to Lite locations; assigned location limits PIN access but does not necessarily hide inventory for other locations.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Expose a role simulation showing effective access by plan and location; measure permission misconfiguration and manager-approval delays.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Permission boundaries should cover Bitcoin tender actions with the same least-privilege and manager-approval pattern; measure unauthorized attempts and approval time.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No Bitcoin-specific POS role is documented; transaction signing or settlement authorization may require distinct controls beyond existing POS roles.
claims.acceptance_test: Configure Pro role to require manager approval for a sensitive operation, then verify staff cannot complete it until authorized manager PIN is entered.

claims.capability: Restrict POS login by assigned location while scope-checking orders
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can limit where staff PINs work and restrict cross-location order access with a separate permission.
claims.trigger: Staff PIN attempts access at a location or staff views orders from another location.
claims.behavior: Assigned locations constrain POS PIN access; staff may still view inventory across locations, while cross-location order viewing/editing requires Manage orders at all locations permission.
preconditions: Staff profile is assigned to POS locations; role and admin scope depend on plan.
qualifiers: Location assignment controls POS login and is not a general inventory-data boundary; Shopify admin access can expose analytics/location data.
recovery_edge_cases: If a staff member cannot use PIN at a location, confirm location assignment and device sync; inventory visibility remains broader by documented design.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make effective visibility by resource and location explicit to staff admins; measure cross-location access errors and training time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Location access and order visibility are tender-independent; ensure Bitcoin settlement records respect identical location scopes.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A payment network does not enforce Shopify's staff location authorization; merchant access controls must remain in application layer.
claims.acceptance_test: Assign staff to one location and confirm PIN denied at another; verify cross-location orders remain restricted unless permission enabled.

claims.capability: Open and close cash-register sessions with expected-vs-counted reconciliation
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can record float and cash movements then compare expected cash with physical drawer count at close.
claims.actor: Cashier or manager with register permissions
claims.trigger: A work interval begins or ends and cash drawer activity must be recorded.
claims.behavior: Register session stores starting float, additions/removals, and final count; cash tracking and session reports summarize activity and compare expected cash with counted drawer cash.
preconditions: Cash tracking session is opened; cash register workflow configured.
qualifiers: Sessions can be managed in POS or admin; location cash-tracking reports available in admin.
recovery_edge_cases: Specific variance-adjustment and reopening procedures were not inspected; do not infer these behaviors.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Present per-event cash movement and expected-vs-counted variance in a closeout review; measure unexplained cash variance and close time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Cash closeout remains a distinct physical-money control; Bitcoin tender can be reconciled in payment totals while leaving cash drawer expectations unchanged.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin is not cash in drawer; mixing BTC settlement into cash variance would confuse custody and accounting. The merchant still needs separate tender reconciliation.
claims.acceptance_test: Open a session with a float, record cash add/remove events, close with a counted balance, and verify report includes expected and counted totals.

claims.capability: Review POS daily performance and staff sales reports on device
claims.merchant_outcome: Manager can compare store metrics to prior week and inspect sales credited to staff.
claims.actor: Manager or staff role granted analytics permission
claims.trigger: User opens Analytics and selects Daily Sales or Sales by staff report.
claims.behavior: Daily Sales compares today with same day last week and presents net sales, average order value, items/order and ranked products/types/staff/net payments; staff report supports date filter and sort.
preconditions: POS Pro location; staff role permits View analytics for device's location.
qualifiers: Daily Sales offers today, yesterday, week/month/quarter/year-to-date ranges; report definitions use net figures after returns/deductions.
recovery_edge_cases: Report availability and staff visibility are permission/plan scoped; broader admin report/export behavior was not examined.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Let managers reconcile POS figures to cash and inventory exceptions from the same daily view; measure time to detect discrepancies.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Tender breakdown should include Bitcoin as its own payment type while preserving net-sales comparisons; measure completeness against transaction ledger without converting away the original amount.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Currency conversion basis and volatile asset accounting can affect monetary comparisons; reports must label denomination, conversion time, and settlement status.
claims.acceptance_test: With analytics access, open Daily Sales and staff report; verify prior-week comparison, net metrics, product/staff rankings, date filtering and sorting.

claims.capability: Select and connect retail hardware to support the merchant's POS workflow
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can choose peripherals for barcode scanning, receipt printing, and cash handling and connect them to POS.
claims.trigger: Merchant configures POS station before opening or adds a peripheral.
claims.behavior: Shopify checklist identifies card reader, barcode scanner/printer, receipt printer, stand, cash drawer and mPOP options; POS Hub provides USB wired connection alternative to Bluetooth.
preconditions: Supported device/hardware availability; network should be configured before hardware pairing.
qualifiers: Supported models and purchase options are country-specific; hardware is optional for processing sales.
recovery_edge_cases: Checklist suggests preparing a spare card reader; exact model-specific pairing and recovery steps are in separate guides not inspected.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide compatibility and connectivity checks before station setup; measure setup failures and hardware disconnects at launch.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Existing readers/scanners/receipt printers can continue serving catalog and receipt workflows with a Bitcoin payment option if payment acceptance is supported; measure successful tender completion on supported hardware.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: The guide does not document Bitcoin reader compatibility; merchant may need a separate device or wallet workflow and must verify local availability/support.
claims.acceptance_test: For a supported market/device, connect a selected peripheral and verify POS detects it and the intended scan/print/cash workflow functions.

claims.capability: Customize POS app, customer display, receipts and app settings in admin editor
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can tailor staff-facing and customer-facing POS presentation and select operational POS settings.
claims.trigger: Merchant sets up devices or refines in-store workflows.
claims.behavior: Admin POS editor configures smart grid/app, lock screen, customer display, printed receipts, default payment options, receipt selection, required checkout information, POS apps/extensions and gift-card issue type; preview supports device themes and receipt sizes.
preconditions: POS editor accessed in Shopify admin; in-store experience section appears after a POS device is set up.
qualifiers: Editor is separate from POS app; apps/extensions can add functionality and may have separate conditions or pricing not reviewed.
recovery_edge_cases: Unsaved changes can be undone/redone; changes must be saved before navigating between editor pages.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show per-location effective configuration and a simpler preview-to-device handoff; measure setup time and configuration drift.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant may configure a Bitcoin payment option or related POS extension if supported; test that customer-facing selection and receipt identify tender and denomination clearly.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Payment apps/extensions are not necessarily native or free; merchant must account for compatibility, privacy, support and any app fees.
claims.acceptance_test: Edit a smart-grid tile or receipt template, preview on tablet/mobile and relevant paper size, save, and confirm the saved setting on POS.

claims.capability: Let customer open merchant privacy policy from customer-facing cart display
claims.merchant_outcome: Customer can review the store's published policy on their own device before completing an in-person transaction.
claims.trigger: Customer taps Privacy Policy on cart-summary display.
claims.behavior: Display presents a QR code linking to store Privacy Policy; customer scans it and can dismiss to return to cart.
preconditions: Store Privacy Policy is published; customer-facing cart summary display is in use.
qualifiers: If no policy is published, button does not display; POS privacy-data handling and export are outside evidence inspected.
recovery_edge_cases: Customer can dismiss QR view and return to cart; no offline policy access behavior documented.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make policy availability and QR readability testable on deployed display devices; measure successful customer access and support requests.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Policy presentation is tender-independent; ensure any Bitcoin payment flow links to the same merchant policy and clearly explains its settlement terms.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A policy link does not answer applicable privacy, refund, or payment disclosures; merchants remain responsible for accurate local terms.
claims.acceptance_test: Publish policy, open POS customer cart summary, tap Privacy Policy, scan displayed QR, and verify return to cart after dismiss.

claims.capability: Collect distinct product configurations through POS UI extension app
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can sell multiple customized configurations of the same base product in a single cart.
claims.actor: POS staff and installed POS UI extension
claims.trigger: Customer requests options such as personalized frame size or named coffee orders.
claims.behavior: An installed app using POS UI Extensions can collect additional product information and support different configurations of one product in the same cart.
preconditions: A POS UI extension app that implements the configuration workflow is installed.
qualifiers: Official quick reference presents this as app-provided; no native modifier editor, supported data model, pricing, or availability terms were documented in reviewed guides.
recovery_edge_cases: If extension is unavailable, guide does not document fallback; app-specific behavior unknown.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Let merchants configure common modifiers with transparent per-choice inventory and price impact; measure order corrections and modifier entry time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Product configuration should be tender-independent; verify all configured variants/modifiers retain line-item identity for Bitcoin orders without forced fiat conversion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Modifier tooling comes from an app in the cited behavior and may carry cost or integration dependencies; payment support does not imply configurator support.
claims.acceptance_test: Install a POS UI extension app supporting options, add two configurations of the same base item to one cart, and verify each carries its selected additional product information.

claims.capability: Display loyalty status from third-party platform as pinned POS customer metafield
claims.merchant_outcome: Staff can view a loyalty tier or other loyalty status on the customer profile at the point of service.
claims.trigger: Staff opens the customer profile at the POS location.
claims.behavior: Admin-created customer metafield can be pinned and displayed in POS; Shopify's example specifically says tiered loyalty status metafield may be created by a loyalty platform.
preconditions: POS Pro location; metafield configured and pinned in admin; staff has View metafields permission.
qualifiers: This is profile display, not a documented native points accrual/redemption engine; loyalty platform app is the named source of status, app pricing/features unknown.
recovery_edge_cases: Unpinned fields are not displayed; POS Lite locations do not display pinned metafields.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Expose reward balance and redemption eligibility as verifiable POS context with clear app provenance; measure reward lookup time and incorrect redemptions.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Loyalty status should follow customer and merchant rules across payment types; verify Bitcoin sales accrue equivalent loyalty when merchant enables it, without requiring fiat conversion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: The cited status field depends on an external loyalty platform and POS Pro visibility; rewards accounting is not native POS evidence here.
claims.acceptance_test: Configure/pin a loyalty-status metafield from a loyalty platform and confirm authorized POS Pro staff can view it on the customer profile.

claims.capability: Limit register session to one open session per POS device and interval
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can associate drawer tracking to a device and close sessions on regular operating or staff-shift boundaries.
claims.trigger: A device starts, tracks, or closes cash/register session.
claims.behavior: Only one register session can be open on each device; sessions created on one device are not visible on other devices; guide recommends closing at regular intervals because long sessions can make expected-cash/discrepancy reports inaccurate.
preconditions: Register sessions activated on device.
qualifiers: Session tracks cash and other tender sales; it is not long-term payment reporting or a staff timecard.
recovery_edge_cases: After app reset/reinstall sessions may not display locally; POS Pro location can access all sessions from admin.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make device-bound session boundaries and cross-device history explicit; measure sessions left open beyond shift and reconciliation errors.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin payments should appear in payment tracking by tender while session cash counts remain physical cash only; test cross-device reconciliation and denomination labeling.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Register session does not equal employee hours or Bitcoin settlement ledger; distinct records are needed.
claims.acceptance_test: Open a register session on device A, verify device B does not show it as its local session, close at shift end, and confirm session report.

claims.capability: Control manual or automatic cash drawer opening and record manual-open reason
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can limit drawer access and record why staff opened the drawer outside a cash sale.
claims.trigger: Staff opens connected drawer manually or cash transaction triggers automatic opening.
claims.behavior: Drawer can open manually or automatically after cash transactions; admin can require reason codes for manual opening; drawer attaches one-to-one with POS device via receipt printer.
preconditions: Compatible cash drawer and receipt printer connected; staff has Open drawer permission for POS open action.
qualifiers: In multi-drawer setups, automatic open only works through device's default printer; Sweden auto-open setting is always on per source.
recovery_edge_cases: Troubleshoot cable, printer paper, pairing and default printer when drawer fails; drawer must be tested through connectivity menu.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show drawer-device-printer mapping and reason prompt consistently; measure unexplained opens and connection failures.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Drawer behavior applies to physical cash tender; Bitcoin transaction must not trigger cash drawer unless merchant deliberately configures a separate workflow.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Drawer controls do not secure a Bitcoin wallet or payment authorization; payment hardware and custody controls remain separate.
claims.acceptance_test: With permission and supported setup, test manual opening with required reason and cash-sale auto-open through default printer; verify drawer opens and event is recorded.

claims.capability: Request and export customer-related data to respond to a valid access request
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can provide a copy of available personal data upon an eligible customer access/data-portability request.
claims.trigger: Customer requests access or portability under applicable rules.
claims.behavior: For a selected customer, admin can request customer data from visits processed by Shopify through Customers > profile > More actions > Request customer data; refresh profile to access data, with copy also emailed to store owner. Merchant may provide it when legally required or consistent with store policy. Customer-profile export is a separately permissioned action.
preconditions: User has Request data or Export customer profile permission; merchant determines applicable legal rights and may verify identity.
qualifiers: Shopify-processed store visit data and customer profile export are distinct datasets/actions; response scope depends on law and available Shopify data.
recovery_edge_cases: Identity verification may be needed; POS-specific retention/export behavior is not described by this guide.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show data sources and export scope in one request checklist; measure incomplete responses and turnaround time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Data export should include customer-linked Bitcoin transaction records where merchant holds them and authorized law permits; measure completeness without exposing wallet secrets.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Public blockchain data and merchant customer profiles are different datasets; exporting them together risks over-disclosure and should distinguish pseudonymous chain data.
claims.acceptance_test: With permitted role, submit a test customer data request, refresh and review available data, separately export profile data if authorized, and verify output is tied to the correct customer.

claims.capability: Process customer erasure request and configure regional privacy notices
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can manage a customer data erasure request and publish privacy/cookie/data-sharing notices appropriate to configured regions.
claims.trigger: Customer requests erasure or merchant configures privacy notices for markets.
claims.behavior: Authorized admin requests erasure from customer profile; Shopify processes it for the merchant and removes personal data from store and installed apps/channels, while some sale facts remain visible in admin. Admin configures automated/manual privacy policy, cookie banner and data-sharing opt-out page by region; prior privacy policies can be exported from the two-year archive.
preconditions: Staff has Erase personal data permission for erasure workflow; region settings configured; legal obligations assessed.
qualifiers: Shopify does not erase data from customer's separate relationship with Shop/Shop Pay or other companies with whom merchant shared data; automated settings are not legal advice and rules vary by jurisdiction.
recovery_edge_cases: Admin-submitted erasure can be canceled within 10 days by store users; erasure for active pre-authorized payments can cancel contracts and prevent remaining charges; erasure differs from deleting full profile and leaves order history.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show which systems/apps receive an erasure request and its processing status; measure unresolved deletion requests and notice misconfiguration.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: A merchant system should separate deletable customer profile data from immutable payment proofs and support lawful minimization; demonstrate request handling without forcing public address identity linkage.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Immutable public-ledger data cannot be erased in the same manner as a customer record; preserve privacy through data minimization and avoid linking identities to addresses unnecessarily.
claims.acceptance_test: Submit an authorized erasure request, verify pending request and 10-day cancel window, review data still retained, and configure/export a regional privacy notice version.

claims.capability: Bulk import/export product and variant data through structured CSV
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can migrate or update many product and variant records together, including identifiers such as barcodes.
claims.trigger: Merchant imports a product catalog or exports catalog for bulk changes.
claims.behavior: Shopify product CSV exports/imports product and variant details; a product CSV import cannot be canceled once started and import history is not available, though activity log can show recent changes; inventory for multiple locations uses separate inventory CSV.
preconditions: CSV follows required headers/dependencies and UTF-8 formatting; product updates include URL handle and title; variant rows include handle and option values.
qualifiers: Product import can overwrite details; exported sample's Inventory quantity applies only to single-location store; barcode field supports multiple typed values.
recovery_edge_cases: Back up product data before import; failed inventory rows may be emailed if snapshot validation detects changed quantities; import file may fail on stale image URLs or malformed related columns.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Offer a preview/dry-run of changed records and variant mappings before irreversible import; measure import recovery time and catalog mismatch rate.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Product and inventory bulk workflows do not depend on tender; preserve catalog identity for Bitcoin-enabled sales and avoid creating fiat-specific duplicates.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: CSV import is operationally distinct from payment ledger import; do not interpret catalog import as accepting or reconciling Bitcoin payments.
claims.acceptance_test: Export a multi-variant product, update a non-sensitive field and barcode, import it, and verify matching variants while confirming inventory CSV is used for per-location stock.

claims.capability: Distinguish register cash sessions from staff timekeeping records
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can use register sessions to reconcile transaction intervals while avoiding treating them as a payroll timecard.
claims.trigger: Merchant defines shift start/end and needs operational closeout records.
claims.behavior: Shopify documentation describes register sessions as cash/payment records for intervals and describes staff actions/PIN attribution; inspected POS guides do not document native employee clock-in, clock-out, or hours-timesheet behavior.
preconditions: Register session feature enabled; staff use own PIN for action attribution.
qualifiers: No native timekeeping behavior is claimed; dedicated time-clock functionality remains unknown and may require another system/app.
recovery_edge_cases: A register session can remain open and become inaccurate for cash reporting, so it should not be used as a proxy for worked hours.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Link shift planning to register closeout while preserving explicit separation between hours and drawer activity; measure missed closeouts and timekeeping mismatches.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Staff identity/time records should apply equally across all tenders; keep settlement timestamps separate from payroll clock events.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Payment protocols do not supply labor time records; a merchant should not infer hours from blockchain or register transaction activity.
claims.acceptance_test: Confirm a staff PIN action is attributed in POS and a cash session records payment interval; verify no documented employee hours record is generated by these operations.

claims.capability: Assign multiple barcode identifiers to product or variant
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can use supplier, region, or marketplace identifiers to locate the same sellable item.
claims.trigger: Merchant adds or edits a product/variant barcode.
claims.behavior: Merchant can add up to 20 barcodes to a product or variant through admin, mobile camera, bulk editor, or CSV, with an optional type; POS can search any barcode or SKU.
preconditions: Barcode identifiers added to product/variant; barcode value unique on same product/variant.
qualifiers: GTIN requirements may apply to publishing on some sales channels; admin and POS scanner support differ.
recovery_edge_cases: If barcode fails, check it is in Barcode field rather than SKU, matches label, and product is active/unlisted and available on POS channel.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Validate identifier collisions across variants and offer scan-to-add during intake; measure unrecognized barcode lookups.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Barcode identity should map to same item regardless of tender; test that scanning into a Bitcoin transaction selects the identical variant and stock item.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Barcode identifies merchandise, not payment authorization or Bitcoin address; keep those namespaces distinct.
claims.acceptance_test: Assign two distinct barcode types to one variant, scan/search each in POS, and verify both resolve to the correct product/variant.

claims.capability: Resolve product or variant from POS barcode scanner or device camera
claims.merchant_outcome: Staff can add scanned merchandise to cart or locate it for inventory workflows.
claims.trigger: Staff scans a product barcode or SKU in cart/search/inventory workflow.
claims.behavior: Supported scanner in Application mode adds scanned item to cart; external scanner can search products/orders/customers; camera scanner supports products and other listed code types but must be invoked from barcode icon. Variant scan in global search may show parent product and require variant selection.
preconditions: Supported external scanner/camera; correct mode and code field; product is available on POS channel.
qualifiers: Scanner models and compatibility vary; Stocky workflows require HID Keyboard Mode; inventory scan supported only in specific workflows.
recovery_edge_cases: Wrong scan target changes behavior: scanning in search bar searches rather than adding to cart; unrecognized code or pairing failure can be diagnosed by camera scan and connectivity settings.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make scanner mode and scan destination visible before input; measure rescans and wrong-variant additions.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Scanner resolution should be identical before tender selection; ensure the chosen variant and quantity stay attached when Bitcoin payment begins.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Reader/scanner compatibility does not imply Bitcoin payment compatibility; test the payment interface separately.
claims.acceptance_test: Scan SKU in cart with application-mode scanner and in global search with camera; verify add-to-cart vs search behavior and manual variant selection where applicable.

claims.capability: Resume submitted inventory count after POS device interruption
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can continue a count from another device without redoing submitted progress.
claims.trigger: POS device freezes or fails during scheduled count.
claims.behavior: Submitted count sessions are safely synced to Shopify admin; staff can restart app or switch device and continue from preserved submitted progress; they can scan/search to check count status.
preconditions: Quick count workflow; progress has been submitted/synced.
qualifiers: Untracked or unassigned products may not appear and should be noted then assigned to location in admin after count.
recovery_edge_cases: Only already submitted progress is documented as preserved; unsent in-progress entries are not guaranteed.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show last successful sync and unsaved count state before device handoff; measure duplicate/re-entered count rows after device failures.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Count recovery is tender-independent; ensure any stock movement from Bitcoin transactions remains visible when count resumes.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Count sync confirms quantity, not payment settlement; inventory count must remain independent of Bitcoin transaction finality.
claims.acceptance_test: Submit a portion of count, simulate app/device interruption, continue on another POS device, and verify submitted entries remain counted once.

claims.capability: Create a retail location and establish its initial stock availability
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can create a distinct store/warehouse location and decide whether it can fulfill online orders.
claims.trigger: Merchant opens another retail or inventory location.
claims.behavior: Admin adds location name/address; new location's inventory is available to fulfill online orders by default; new products are stocked at the location with quantity zero; inventory can be adjusted by location.
preconditions: User has location management access; active location limit depends on plan.
qualifiers: POS Pro subscription location must be downgraded before location deactivation; fulfillment apps may appear as locations but are not counted toward plan limit.
recovery_edge_cases: Cannot remove all stock where pending orders/transfers exist; deactivation prompts handling assigned inventory/orders/transfers and retains inventory operations at inactive location.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show online-availability and zero-stock defaults prominently at creation; measure unintended fulfillment from new stores and launch setup omissions.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Location assignment should remain consistent for Bitcoin and other sales; prove each tender posts sale and stock movement to selected shop location.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Location setup controls inventory/fulfillment, not payment custody; settlement routing may have separate location rules.
claims.acceptance_test: Create a location, inspect default online-fulfillment setting and zero-stock product state, then disable online fulfillment and confirm setting.

claims.capability: Select POS device location and assign POS subscription per location
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can apply the correct location context and feature plan to each POS device/store.
claims.actor: Store owner or POS setup staff
claims.trigger: POS app is installed or merchant changes location plan.
claims.behavior: Device location is selected in POS settings; Shopify says select correct location so correct taxes apply. Account owner can select POS Pro subscription per location; Pro includes additional retail features at additional monthly cost.
preconditions: User has access to POS setup/location settings; payment reader use may require shop and location countries to match.
qualifiers: POS Pro has extra sales, inventory, reports and staff features; plan/payment availability is country and subscription dependent.
recovery_edge_cases: If wrong location selected, change device location in POS settings; plan changes can be managed individually or in batches up to 250 locations.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide a device setup check that confirms location, country and plan before opening; measure mislocated orders and reader incompatibility.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin payment and reporting should inherit the selected merchant location; test correct stock and accounting location across stores without forced fiat conversion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Shopify's country rule described here is specifically for Shopify card readers and may not apply identically to another payment method; do not assume unsupported scope.
claims.acceptance_test: Switch POS device from one configured location to another, verify displayed location, and inspect that location's POS subscription plan in admin.

claims.capability: Review, export, and remotely close register sessions from admin
claims.merchant_outcome: Manager can reconcile sessions by location/date, retain CSV reports, and recover a session that cannot be closed on POS device.
claims.trigger: Manager reviews register reconciliation or device cannot close a session.
claims.behavior: Admin filters sessions by location and timeframe, opens session/net-payments/activity reports, exports open session activity or closed session reports, and can remotely close a session after entering cash counted and remaining drawer balance.
preconditions: User has POS channel access; session was opened in POS; report export permissions available.
qualifiers: Admin cannot open a new session; POS Pro required for cross-location cash tracking reports described separately.
recovery_edge_cases: Closing a session is irreversible; when a transaction is in progress, next completed transaction automatically opens a new session.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide a remote-close confirmation with in-flight transaction and next-session impact; measure unresolved open sessions and audit corrections.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Include Bitcoin tender in payment report export with denomination and settlement state while keeping counted cash input physical; measure ledger-to-session reconciliation.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Cash session closeout does not settle Bitcoin and cannot undo a public transaction; reconcile the systems without conflating balances.
claims.acceptance_test: Filter sessions by location/date, export an open session activity report, remotely close an eligible session with counted cash, and verify the closure is logged and cannot be reopened.

claims.capability: Compare cash tracking discrepancies and payments across POS Pro locations
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can find opening/closing cash discrepancies and export cash session summaries by location and date.
claims.trigger: Manager reviews cash reconciliation for one or multiple locations.
claims.behavior: Cash tracking report summarizes opening/closing discrepancies, gross/refund/net cash payments, and session list; supports location/date filters, sort and CSV export/print.
preconditions: Location is on POS Pro; staff has View payment register session history and View payment register sessions in POS channel permissions.
qualifiers: Cash-rounding regions include rounded payments in report; report shows cash/till metrics rather than general tender settlement details.
recovery_edge_cases: Mismatch definition compares previous closing count to new opening count and session expected cash to final count.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Flag repeated discrepancies across registers and annotate verified causes; measure unresolved discrepancy rate and time-to-review.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Preserve one Bitcoin payment-type line in broader payment summaries while leaving cash discrepancy computations tied only to drawer cash; verify cross-report totals.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Cash tracking is not a Bitcoin accounting report; a linked settlement report is needed to reconcile wallet receipts and merchant books.
claims.acceptance_test: With permissions at Pro location, filter by date and location, compare session discrepancy summary, export sessions, and verify totals match underlying register rows.

claims.capability: Choose supported card reader and connection hardware by country/device
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can select hardware that works with its location, payment processor, and POS device.
claims.trigger: Merchant plans a POS station or replaces a reader.
claims.behavior: Shopify publishes reader models by region and supported hardware by device; Shopify-supported readers require supported country and Shopify Payments, while external terminals use separate provider accounts and have limited Shopify transaction detail integration.
preconditions: Country/payment processor and compatible POS device are known; available hardware list checked.
qualifiers: Hardware-store availability varies by country; external terminal transaction is manually marked paid and POS only displays status without transaction details in described unsupported-country workflow.
recovery_edge_cases: For reliable USB hardware the POS Hub can reduce Bluetooth disconnections; model-specific troubleshooting not covered by this claim.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Expose region/device/processor compatibility before purchase and warn about reduced external-terminal detail; measure mis-purchases and reconciliation gaps.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Merchant may use compatible external wallet/payment terminal alongside POS if they can reconcile status and order; validate exact supported hardware and avoid assuming native integration.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No Bitcoin reader or processor compatibility is documented; external terminal manual marking sacrifices detailed synchronization, and merchant must verify support without forced fiat conversion.
claims.acceptance_test: Check a selected model against official country/device table; verify reader is supported for payment provider or external terminal status/manual marking path is understood.

claims.capability: Run scheduled, staff-attributed stock count and review before quantities change
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can delegate physical counts without allowing staff to directly change inventory and approve only reviewed quantities.
claims.actor: Inventory manager and assigned POS staff
claims.trigger: Manager creates a count for a location and staff count listed products.
claims.behavior: Admin creates one-location product list; POS Pro staff scan or enter on-hand quantities, each item is attributed to staff, and staff request review; manager reviews/approves/rejects before inventory updates.
preconditions: POS Pro; count created in desktop admin and assigned to location; staff has Perform inventory counts permission; network connection.
qualifiers: Only listed items can be counted; multiple staff can count concurrently and counts combine; stale products changed during count are marked outdated.
recovery_edge_cases: Staff can continue other products and request review when an item becomes outdated; each location needs separate count.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Display expected quantity, stale-change signal, and reviewer reconciliation in one queue; measure rejected counts and time to approve.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Inventory count approval is payment-independent; verify approved stock reflects all tender sales exactly once, including Bitcoin sales.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Stock counts do not resolve payment finality; manager approval and inventory ledger remain separate from wallet settlement.
claims.acceptance_test: Create an admin count for a location, assign staff, count several listed items concurrently, request review, approve one and reject another, then verify only approved quantities update.

claims.capability: Create and update specific product variants with per-variant values
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can offer valid combinations while setting distinct price, SKU, barcode, inventory, image, shipping and location values per variant.
claims.trigger: Merchant introduces another product option value or edits an existing combination.
claims.behavior: Merchant adds named options and values (up to three options and 2,048 variants); can add single variants, duplicate variants/bulk combinations, or connect options to category metafields; individual variants can be edited or bulk-edited.
preconditions: Product is created in admin or Shopify app; a new variant must have at least one new option value.
qualifiers: Adding a new option value generates combinations; manually adding/duplicating one variant does not create every possible combination; variant editor UI may differ during rollout.
recovery_edge_cases: Exact duplicate variant cannot be saved; stop-selling can be done by unpublishing to preserve history rather than deleting; variant settings may need per-variant adjustment.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Preview generated variant combinations and inherited fields before saving; measure duplicate variants, missing price/SKU and setup time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Variant-level identity and inventory should be shared across Bitcoin and other tender; validate each variant and its stock mapping across tenders without fiat-only product duplication.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Variant metadata does not define settlement currency; any Bitcoin price presentation must preserve merchant-selected catalog price and explicit quote basis.
claims.acceptance_test: Add size/color options and inspect generated combinations; manually add a unique variant, try an exact duplicate, edit a price and location quantity, and verify expected save/rejection outcomes.

claims.capability: Create and process an inventory transfer with shipment tracking
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can stage a transfer, inspect source/destination quantity effects, then commit stock movement and track shipments.
claims.trigger: Merchant replenishes another store or receives supplier stock.
claims.behavior: Admin creates draft transfer with optional origin/destination, products and quantities; draft is editable and uncommitted; processing moves through ready/in-progress/transferred/canceled states; shipment can carry tracking, expected arrival, barcode and cost details.
preconditions: User has admin inventory transfer access; source/destination locations exist or blank endpoint represents external party.
qualifiers: Transfer quantity at destination does not automatically activate product there; receiving/activation controls sellability; bulk transfer CSV can overwrite variant quantity already on existing transfer.
recovery_edge_cases: Draft transfer can be deleted; ready-to-ship cannot be deleted and must be canceled; canceled committed quantity returns available at origin.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Preview source availability, destination activation, and shipment commitments in a single review before processing; measure transfer cancellation and unstocked-at-destination errors.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Stock movement is tender-independent; preserve location reconciliation and use Bitcoin only as a separate settlement rail for sales, without forced fiat conversion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A transfer is an inventory movement, not a payment; no Bitcoin settlement behavior should be inferred from it.
claims.acceptance_test: Create draft transfer between locations, inspect quantity effect without commitment, process it and add shipment details; verify transfer status and destination product activation state.

claims.capability: Find and attach existing customer profile to POS cart
claims.merchant_outcome: Staff can connect a sale to the correct customer while retaining cart context.
claims.trigger: Customer is identified by name/email at checkout or during service.
claims.behavior: POS supports customer search from global search, navigation, and Add Customer screen; selecting a result attaches the profile to cart/order, and customer can be removed from order.
preconditions: POS app online; existing profile available; customer lookup permissions as configured.
qualifiers: Global search keeps cart visible; result may be searched by another matching attribute; POS Pro can require missing info during checkout.
recovery_edge_cases: If wrong profile attached, staff can remove customer from order and select correct profile.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show distinguishing customer details and match reason before attaching; measure duplicate/wrong customer associations.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Profile attachment is independent of tender; allow optional association for Bitcoin sales without requiring identity for payment.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Identity association can improve service but introduces privacy sensitivity; payment method should not force customer lookup.
claims.acceptance_test: Search by email from global bar and Add Customer screen, attach matching profile, then remove and verify cart remains available.

claims.capability: Edit customer contact details and marketing preferences in POS
claims.merchant_outcome: Staff can correct customer data and preserve current email/SMS marketing choices.
claims.actor: POS staff with customer edit permission
claims.trigger: Customer asks staff to update address/contact or marketing preference.
claims.behavior: Staff search customer, open profile edit, update supported details, choose email or SMS marketing where corresponding contact is present, and save.
preconditions: Staff has View customer details and Edit customer details permissions; email/SMS field exists for respective marketing option.
qualifiers: This claim covers POS edit flow; profile data access controlled by role.
recovery_edge_cases: Marketing option absent if profile has no corresponding email or phone; changes require Save.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show consent history and last update source beside preferences; measure marketing preference corrections and unauthorized changes.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Customer preference management must remain tender-neutral and should not be conditioned on Bitcoin payment.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Payment rail provides no basis for marketing consent; merchant must preserve independent opt-in controls.
claims.acceptance_test: With both permissions, edit contact details and turn on email/SMS only when corresponding fields exist; save and confirm profile values.

claims.capability: View and share customer gift-card balance/history from POS
claims.merchant_outcome: Staff can verify remaining gift-card value and transaction history for a customer and communicate card details.
claims.trigger: Customer asks about a gift card linked to their profile.
claims.behavior: Staff search customer, open all gift cards, inspect selected card details, print/email/text information, or deactivate card; deactivation cannot be undone.
preconditions: Customer profile and gift card exist; POS staff can access profile.
qualifiers: This is gift-card account lookup, not gift-card sale or payment acceptance.
recovery_edge_cases: Deactivate action is irreversible per guide; verify card before action.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Require a clear irreversible-action confirmation and show balance/history before sharing; measure mistaken deactivations and lookup duration.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Gift-card balance servicing should be independent of payment tender; Bitcoin sales may coexist without changing a gift card's stored value unless merchant records an explicit redemption.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Stored-value liabilities differ from Bitcoin balances; keep the customer's gift card ledger distinct from any wallet settlement.
claims.acceptance_test: Find profile, review gift-card balance and transaction history, send details through one supported method, and confirm deactivation warning indicates irreversible change.

claims.capability: Receive supplier purchase-order quantities through its linked inventory transfer
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can reconcile accepted, rejected, canceled, or partial supplier deliveries into destination inventory.
claims.trigger: Ordered goods arrive from a supplier.
claims.behavior: Staff open the PO-linked transfer and assign quantities to Accept, Reject, or Cancel actions; accepted goods become available at destination, rejected quantities remain recorded but unavailable, canceled quantities are removed, and transfer stays In progress until all quantities are accounted for.
preconditions: Purchase order is marked Ordered and linked inventory transfer exists; destination location and inventory tracking are configured.
qualifiers: Receipt is on the transfer, not directly on the purchase order; individual shipments can be received separately; scanner or manual quantities supported.
recovery_edge_cases: Multiple actions can be recorded for same item; notes can record reason. Stocky POS PO extension page is historical because Stocky ended 2026-08-31; current guide specifies Shopify admin transfer receipt.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show expected/received/rejected balance across each shipment and action before save; measure unaccounted supplier units and receipt corrections.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Supplier receipt changes inventory independently of customer payment rail; preserve the same destination stock behavior when merchandise later sells for Bitcoin without forced conversion.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Supplier purchase orders capture commercial terms and inventory receipt, not settlement; Bitcoin supplier payment accounting is not established by this guide.
claims.acceptance_test: Mark a PO ordered, receive linked transfer with accepted/rejected/canceled partial quantities, and verify only accepted goods are available at destination and status remains in progress for outstanding units.

claims.capability: Attribute high-risk POS operations to performing staff for investigation
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can investigate who performed a sensitive register action such as void, refund, manual discount, or customer record access.
claims.trigger: Merchant reviews suspected error or high-risk POS action.
claims.behavior: Shopify POS activity log records attribution for listed high-risk actions and can be reviewed through the Shopify admin activity-log path.
preconditions: Staff actions were performed under individual staff PINs; administrator can access relevant activity log.
qualifiers: Store activity logs have separate retention/export characteristics; not every admin action is recorded and exportability varies by log version.
recovery_edge_cases: Shopify says deleted-staff attribution may display as Shopify deleted [staff name] in current store log; inspect relevant order/customer/timeline as needed.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Provide direct links from staff action to order/customer/session context and retention status; measure investigation completion time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin sales and operational actions should be attributed to staff the same way; do not equate on-chain signer with POS staff identity.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Staff activity log does not prove who controlled an external wallet or authorized a separate device; record external transaction reference in merchant records.
claims.acceptance_test: Perform a high-risk action under a named staff PIN and locate the attributed event in POS activity log or related order timeline.

claims.capability: Create location-specific POS smart-grid templates and assign a default
claims.merchant_outcome: Merchant can standardize POS shortcuts across stores and tailor layouts by location.
claims.trigger: Merchant configures POS layouts for new locations or revises a store workflow.
claims.behavior: Admin can create, rename, duplicate, search, and assign multiple templates; each location has one template, and one default applies to new/unassigned locations.
preconditions: POS device set up to expose in-store experience editor; admin has product-view and location settings permission.
qualifiers: POS staff can edit local grid with Customize smart grid permission; editing a shared template from a single location creates a local copy; app tiles require POS-integrated app.
recovery_edge_cases: Deleting a template is irreversible and assigned locations revert to default; duplicate template does not copy original location assignments.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show template assignment and change impact before saving/deleting; measure misassigned devices and layout drift.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: A Bitcoin payment tile may be added through supported app integration while keeping standard product and inventory tiles; verify controls and fees before deployment.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No Bitcoin tile is documented natively; an app integration may be paid and requires separate support/compatibility validation.
claims.acceptance_test: Create a new template, assign to one location, set another as default, and verify new location uses default while duplicate template has no inherited assignment.

limitations: This is a bounded review of public Shopify Help Center material accessed 2026-11-17, not a live Shopify POS account, hardware, or transaction test; documentation does not establish verified compatibility.

The parent POS overview and selected assigned branches were reviewed; coverage entries identify exclusions and unresolved topics. This bundle does not claim exhaustive review of every Shopify guide, country-specific rule, plan, device, app, or backend condition.

Product configuration is documented as available through POS UI Extension apps, but a native modifier editor was not found in the official pages inspected; individual app capability and pricing remain unknown. Loyalty examples use apps/Flow and metafields rather than documenting native POS points accrual/redemption. Privacy guides cover merchant requests and settings but do not specify POS-specific customer-data retention/export behavior.

A native POS employee time clock or timesheet behavior was not found in the inspected staff/register guides; register sessions describe cash/payment tracking intervals and are not evidence of payroll hours functionality. This is a documented-evidence boundary, not proof that no Shopify or third-party timekeeping product exists.

Some historically indexed Stocky guides remain publicly readable, but Shopify says Stocky ended on 2026-08-31. Their workflows are not represented as currently available; current built-in Shopify inventory and purchase-order guides are used for present-day behaviors.

Third-party POS apps/extensions and paid add-ons are not presumed native or included. Where present, the source says an extension/app is required, but its price and vendor behavior were not researched.

Bitcoin hypotheses are design questions only. They neither claim Shopify currently supports Bitcoin in POS nor reject any current merchant workflow; operational proof should cover denomination, authorization, settlement, refunds/liability, reporting, staff permissions, and no forced fiat conversion.
